facts.text: Fairfield grew from the Fairfield Mission, a nineteenth-century outpost established to provide education and religious services for Cherokee settlements.
The Fairfield Mission was originally known as Mulberry Mission in Pope County, Arkansas Territory, before relocating to Indian Territory.
In 1832, the mission in Fairfield established a circulating library with 150 volumes, reportedly the first of its kind in the region.
Fairfield provided neutrality and aid to Cherokee families during factional conflicts and the lead-up to the Cherokee Civil War.
The McLemore Cemetery remains as a lasting landmark of the original mission site and served local Cherokee families into the late nineteenth century.
The Oklahoma Historical Society marked the site of the Fairfield Mission in 1995 to preserve its legacy as an early Protestant outpost.
